title: SLO-aware tokenized retry & hedged-request contract for multi-region failover
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Services and client SDKs currently implement divergent retry/timeouts/backoff policies. In multi-region failover scenarios we've observed double-retries (client + router), unbounded hedged-fanout, and duplicate side-effects when idempotency is not enforced. This has contributed to transient increases in tail latency and several customer-impacting incidents where the surface-level SLO (p99 < 120ms) was missed during regional perturbations.

Goal: Define a single, implementable contract between services, the edge/router layer, and SDKs that: (1) is SLO-aware (adapts retry aggressiveness to route/service SLOs), (2) introduces a tokenized idempotency header for safe retries, (3) specifies hedged-request gating and fanout limits per route, and (4) defines clear interactions with circuit breakers and load-shedding signals. The contract must be forward-compatible and require minimal changes to existing customers when enabled by feature flag.

Why different from prior work: Existing tickets focused on retry semantics or idempotency in isolation. This ticket converges SLO-driven cooldowns, an explicit client-to-runtime handshake via tokenized idempotency, and hedged request safety rules — with operational metrics and a migration plan to safely roll out across hosted/runtime/private deployments.
proposal:
Summary of the proposed contract:

1) Idempotency token (X-RW-Idempotency): opaque v1 token generated by client SDK for operations that are not strictly read-only. Token is RFC-safe (UUIDv4 or hashed user-supplied token). Servers MUST persist idempotency outcomes for a configurable TTL and return 409 + canonical result when duplicate detected.

2) Retry classification header (X-RW-Retry-Intent): values = 'safe-retry' | 'speculative' | 'no-retry'. Clients set intent; routers and runtimes may override based on SLO. 'safe-retry' requires an idempotency token; 'speculative' allowed only for read-only and subject to hedged fanout limits.

3) Hedged-request gating: Router maintains per-route hedgedConcurrency budget (default 2). Hedging allowed only when route SLO headroom > threshold (default: 15% p99 headroom). Router emits hedged decisions in traces.

4) Backoff/timeouts: SDKs adopt SLO-driven base timeout = min(route_target_latency * 3, 30s). Retry attempts: up to 3 for 'safe-retry' with exponential backoff base 2x and cap 5s, full jitter +/-25%. For cross-region failover, clients backoff an extra random delay 100-500ms to reduce synchronized fanout.

5) Circuit-breaker interaction: Services expose CB state via X-RW-CB header values 'closed'|'degraded'|'open'. Clients and routers must avoid retries against 'open' endpoints and prefer fallback region or toss error to caller.

6) Load-shedding semantics: When runtime signals overload (503 + Retry-After or custom X-RW-Shed: 'soft'|'hard'), clients may back off aggressively; SDKs convert soft shed into adaptive retry with longer backoffs, but preserve idempotency safety windows.

7) Observability contract: Standardized metrics/tags: rw.retry.attempts, rw.retry.policy, rw.hedge.fanout, rw.idempotency.duplicate, rw.slo.headroom. These must be emitted by routers, runtime, and SDK telemetry for cross-product dashboards.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Tokenized idempotency vs storing full request: token keeps wire small and allows server-side canonicalization. Tradeoff: requires server-side storage TTL and coordination for long-running ops.
- Hedging default budget tuned low (2) to limit downstream amplification; we accept some latency regressions for small percentage of requests in exchange for better p99 under high variance workloads.
- SLO-driven decisions: adds complexity (we must surface reliable headroom metrics) but reduces unnecessary hedging/retries when service is near capacity.
- Backwards-compatibility: default behavior is conservative (no speculative retries) until clients opt-in to new headers. This delays full benefits but avoids breaking existing traffic.
api_examples:
Request (safe retry): POST /charge HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-RW-Idempotency: a12f4b6c-4d3e-4a2b-9c1e-7a6b8d2f0c9e
X-RW-Retry-Intent: safe-retry
X-RW-Client-Timeout: 300ms
Router -> runtime example when hedged: trace metadata includes rw.hedge.fanout=2 and X-RW-Hedged: true

Server duplicate response: HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Idempotency-Status: duplicate
{ "result": "<canonical-result>" }
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (JS/Python/Go) implement X-RW-Idempotency and X-RW-Retry-Intent headers and default backoff algorithms behind a feature flag
Router honors hedgedConcurrency budget and exposes rw.hedge.fanout in traces
Runtime stores idempotency outcomes with TTL and returns canonical duplicate responses (409 + canonical payload) within 99% of replay window
End-to-end test demonstrating reduced duplicate side-effects in simulated multi-region failover (target: >90% reduction vs current baseline)
Dashboards show rw.slo.headroom driving hedging decisions; no SLO regressions in canary region for 48h
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement headers in SDKs behind ff, emit telemetry metrics. Add router feature flag to log hedging decisions without enforcement. Phase 2 (3 weeks): enable router hedging in canary region with low budget and runtime idempotency storage. Phase 3 (4 weeks): expand to additional regions, monitor rw.idempotency.duplicate and rw.retry.attempts, iterate. Phase 4: flip default for non-enterprise routes after 6 weeks of stable telemetry. Rollback: disable router hedging and remove SDK feature flag if duplicates > threshold or SLO regressions observed.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for SDK header generation, jitter/backoff math.
- Integration tests simulating transient 5xx from primary region and observing client behavior (hedging vs retry).
- Chaos test: inject 30% increased latency in primary region, verify canary hedging reduces p99 without inflating duplicate side-effects.
- Load test: validate hedged fanout budget protects downstream runtime under concurrency spike.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: servers fail to persist idempotency outcomes causing duplicate side-effects. Mitigation: start with short TTL and restrict safe-retry to non-destructive ops during initial rollout. Risk: misconfigured SLO headroom metric leads to over-hedging. Mitigation: require a manual override and conservative defaults; dashboards with alerts when headroom-driven hedges exceed X% of traffic.
